faqs.question: Can you mail a boo basket to another country?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as every filler is allowed in the post and in the destination. Leave out liquids, perfume, glass and homemade food, keep snacks factory-sealed, and describe each item on the customs form. Royal Mail's Tracked service aims for 5–7 working days worldwide.

faqs.question: Will chocolate melt in a mailed boo basket?
faqs.answer: It can. A 2024 Food Science & Nutrition study notes chocolate softens at 28–32°C and melts at 34–36°C, so a box heading somewhere warm is at risk. Swap in shortbread, ginger biscuits or liquorice for warm addresses.

faqs.question: What should I write on the customs form for a boo basket?
faqs.answer: Name each item specifically, with quantity and material. USPS lists "Gifts" as an unacceptable description and "One scented candle" as acceptable, and says customs may reject, return or destroy a package with vague descriptions.

faqs.question: When should I post a boo basket so it arrives by Halloween?
faqs.answer: Aim for the Friday before: 30 October 2026 or 29 October 2027. With Royal Mail Tracked worldwide (5–7 working days), the latest post date is Wednesday 21 October 2026 or Wednesday 20 October 2027; post a week earlier if food is inside.

faqs.question: Can I put perfume or nail polish in a long distance boo basket?
faqs.answer: No. Australia Post lists perfume and nail polish as flammable liquids that cannot be posted within Australia or overseas. A solid lotion bar or a sealed sheet mask is a safer pamper item.

faqs.question: Can I send homemade Halloween treats abroad?
faqs.answer: Usually not without paperwork. Australia Post's guide for India says foodstuffs need the receiver's permissions and paperwork and FSSAI-compliant shipping, and its International Courier service carries no food at all. Send factory-sealed snacks or order treats locally instead.

faqs.question: Can I include LED candles or fairy lights?
faqs.answer: Only with the battery installed. Australia Post accepts lithium batteries internationally only inside the device, at most two batteries or four cells, and the device must not be able to switch on by accident. Tape the switch off before packing.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to order the treats locally and post only the personal items?
faqs.answer: Often. Royal Mail's online prices on 14 October 2026 listed a Tracked large letter up to 250g at £12.05 to World Zone 3, against £20.20 for a 2kg small parcel to the USA. Food bought in their country also skips customs.

faqs.question: What if the boo basket arrives after Halloween?
faqs.answer: Send something that lands on the night anyway, such as a Halloween page shared as a link. The premium Halloween page can hold an unlock time, so until then the link shows only their name and a countdown.

faqs.question: How do I make a mailed boo basket feel personal?
faqs.answer: Add something that carries you, not just a theme. In Jurkane-Hobein's interviews with 19 long-distance partners in Latvia, one described a T-shirt with the partner's scent bringing them close. Seal a worn shirt in a zip bag on the day you post.

faqs.question: Can I make a Halloween page for my long-distance partner with a voice note?
faqs.answer: Yes. The premium Halloween page on SubhSandesh takes about 10 minutes and holds a voice note of up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and a reply box for one answer of up to 280 characters. You send it as a private link.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Long Distance Boo Basket: How to Mail One That Arrives Intact

A long distance boo basket is a Halloween treat box that has to survive about a week in the post, so build it from things that cannot melt, leak, shatter or fail customs, and name every item on the declaration. Time it to land on the last working day before 31 October, then send a link for the night itself. On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, and 92.1% of our "I miss you" pages carry at least one "open when" letter (197 of 214 pages, a two-month sample that is not Halloween data). Below: six things that fail in transit, how to pack and declare the box, mailing-by dates for 2026 and 2027, and the order-to-their-door alternative.

## What is a long distance boo basket?

A long distance boo basket is a boo basket that travels by post or courier instead of being left on a doorstep. The idea is unchanged, but each filler must now cope with sorting belts, cargo holds and a customs officer.

Royal Mail's [International Tracked service](https://www.royalmail.com/sending/international/international-tracked) aims for 3–5 working days to Europe and 5–7 worldwide (read 14 October 2026). That week in a box changes three decisions: the container, the food and the note. A wicker basket rarely survives; a strong shipping carton with a collapsible fabric basket folded flat inside does.

## What survives the post? 6 things that fail in transit

Each entry below follows one pattern: what goes wrong, the rule that applies, the swap, and how to pack it.

### 1. Chocolate bound for a warm address

**What goes wrong:** chocolate begins to soften and lose shape at 28–32°C and melts between 34 and 36°C, when it sticks to its wrapper, according to a [2024 study in Food Science & Nutrition](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11561827) by Laughter, Brown and Anantheswaran. A parked van can pass that easily.

**The rule:** no postal operator we checked bans chocolate; heat is the risk.

**The swap:** for a warm destination, choose shortbread, ginger biscuits or liquorice. Keep chocolate for cool-climate addresses.

**Pack it:** sealed bag, centre of the box, away from the walls.

### 2. Perfume, nail polish and anything that pours

**What goes wrong:** bottles leak under pressure changes and soak everything else.

**The rule:** Australia Post's [prohibited and restricted items page](https://auspost.com.au/personal/sending/sending-guidelines/dangerous-prohibited-items) lists nail polish, paint and perfume as flammable liquids that cannot be posted within Australia or overseas.

**The swap:** a solid lotion bar or a sheet face mask in its sealed foil sachet.

**Pack it:** even solids go in a zip bag, in case the box gets wet.

### 3. Glass and ceramic decorations

**What goes wrong:** a mug or a ceramic pumpkin cracks at the first drop from a conveyor.

**The rule:** fragile items may be posted, but the cover is small: Royal Mail's Tracked service includes compensation up to £50, or up to £250 for £3.10 extra.

**The swap:** felt or wooden decorations, which reach the door looking the way they left.

**Pack it:** at least 5 cm of crumpled paper on every side.

### 4. Battery-powered candles and lights

**What goes wrong:** a switch knocked on in transit drains the battery or warms the box.

**The rule:** Australia Post accepts lithium batteries internationally only when they are installed in the device, at most two batteries or four cells, and the device cannot switch on by accident.

**The swap:** an LED tea light with the battery fitted and its plastic pull-tab still in place.

**Pack it:** tape the switch off and wrap the light on its own.

### 5. Homemade and fresh food

**What goes wrong:** border inspectors cannot verify what is inside a home-baked tin, so it is the first thing removed.

**The rule:** Australia Post's [guide to posting to India](https://auspost.com.au/personal/sending/parcels/sending-internationally/international-post-guide/india) says foodstuffs need the receiver to hold the necessary permissions and paperwork and the sender to follow FSSAI guidelines, and that food of any kind is prohibited on its International Courier service.

**The swap:** factory-sealed snacks with the ingredient label intact, or treats bought in their country (see below).

**Pack it:** original packaging only.

### 6. A worn T-shirt, the filler that travels best

**What goes wrong:** almost nothing. It weighs little, cannot break and does not melt.

**The rule:** describe it plainly on the form, and check the destination's rules on used clothing.

**Why it works:** Iveta Jurkane-Hobein's Uppsala thesis interviewed 19 people in Latvia whose partners lived more than 45 km away. One described a T-shirt carrying the partner's scent bringing them close, part of what she called imagined intimacy, according to a [2016 review in Nordisk Østforum](https://tidsskriftet-nof.no/index.php/noros/article/view/465) (in Danish).

**Pack it:** seal it in a zip bag the day you post, so the scent holds.

## How to pack and declare a mailed boo basket

Pack in three layers: the soft basket at the bottom, the heavy sealed snacks in the middle, and the T-shirt and letter on top as a cushion. Fill every gap so nothing moves when you shake the box, then tape every seam, not only the lid.

The customs form is where most baskets get stuck. USPS's [customs forms page](https://www.usps.com/international/customs-forms.htm) now requires a specific description of every item in every international package, including small personal gifts. It lists "Gifts" as an unacceptable description and "One scented candle" as an acceptable one, and warns that customs officials may reject, return or destroy a package that falls short.

Write lines like these:

- Two packets of factory-sealed shortbread biscuits
- One cotton T-shirt, worn, personal item
- One felt pumpkin decoration
- One LED tea light, battery installed
- One handwritten letter and four printed photos

Royal Mail asks senders to check its own prohibitions and the rules of the destination country, and it points anyone sending gifts to the USA to a separate update page. Australia Post's guide for the United States tells senders to confirm restrictions on foodstuffs, alcoholic beverages and plant products with local authorities before posting.

## Mailing-by dates for 31 October in 2026 and 2027

Halloween falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, so the box should land by Friday 30 October 2026 or Friday 29 October 2027. The table counts back from those Fridays using Royal Mail's Tracked delivery aims, which are targets, not guarantees.

| Route | Delivery aim | Last post date, Halloween 2026 | Last post date, Halloween 2027 | Safer date with a customs week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Royal Mail Tracked to Ireland, France, Germany and seven more | 3–4 working days | Mon 26 Oct | Mon 25 Oct | Mon 19 Oct 2026 / Mon 18 Oct 2027 |
| Royal Mail Tracked, rest of Europe | 3–5 working days | Fri 23 Oct | Fri 22 Oct | Fri 16 Oct 2026 / Fri 15 Oct 2027 |
| Royal Mail Tracked, worldwide | 5–7 working days | Wed 21 Oct | Wed 20 Oct | Wed 14 Oct 2026 / Wed 13 Oct 2027 |
| A Halloween page sent as a link | Instant | 31 Oct | 31 Oct | Build 5–10 minutes before |

Post on the safer date if food is inside, since that is the part customs opens. Senders outside the UK should count back from their own operator's published estimates in the same way.

Most people plan later than a parcel allows. We have no Halloween data, but on Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we measured (n = 89), 55.7% of the 79 greeting pages finished in time were built on the day itself. A boo basket cannot be posted that late.

## The order-to-their-door alternative

Split the basket in two. Order the treats from a shop or grocery app in their country for delivery to their door, then post only the personal, flat part: the T-shirt, a letter and photos.

The numbers favour it. Royal Mail's online prices (14 October 2026) list a Tracked large letter up to 250g at £9.90 to Europe and £12.05 to World Zone 3, against £20.20 for a 2kg small parcel to the USA. If the shirt and letter fit the large-letter size, the food never meets a customs form.

The trade-off is control. You cannot check what the shop packs, the brands will be theirs rather than yours, and you need their delivery address and a slot when they are home. Pick snacks you know they buy, because local favourites beat imported novelty.

## A Halloween page they open on the night

The parcel lands before Halloween; the moment itself can still arrive on the night. The [interactive haunted-house Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes: your names, a letter, up to six photos and a word to carve. They knock three times, carve a jack-o'-lantern, find your photos behind fogged portraits and read your letter by flashlight, and you get an email the first time they answer.

For a partner far away, the [premium Halloween page with a voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) suits better and takes about 10 minutes. It carries a voice note of up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos, a reply box for one answer of up to 280 characters, and an optional unlock time; until then the link shows only their name and a countdown.

Long-distance senders on SubhSandesh are the most private group we measure: 43.5% of "I miss you" senders password-protect the page, against 38.5% platform-wide, and 28.0% set a reunion date for the countdown (n = 214, since July 2026). For the months after Halloween, an [I miss you page with a reunion countdown](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) keeps the thread going.

## When a mailed boo basket is the wrong choice

Skip the parcel when fewer than seven working days remain before Friday 30 October 2026 (or Friday 29 October 2027) and the address is outside Europe. Skip it, too, when the destination restricts food and you cannot confirm the rules; order locally instead.

A page loses in other cases. It cannot carry a scent, a fabric or anything they can hold, and both Halloween pages are English-only greeting pages for one person, not a gift service. If your partner dislikes screens, post the letter alone and let the paper do the work.

## Sources

- Royal Mail, "International Tracked", undated, delivery aims and prices read 14 October 2026.
- Laughter, Brown and Anantheswaran, "Effect of curing conditions on heat resistance in white chocolate", Food Science & Nutrition, 9 July 2024.
- Australia Post, "Prohibited and restricted items", undated, read 14 October 2026.
- Australia Post, "International post guide: India", undated, read 14 October 2026.
- Anna Sofie Bach, review of Jurkane-Hobein, "I Imagine You Here Now", Nordisk Østforum, 21 June 2016.
- USPS, "Customs Forms", undated, read 14 October 2026.
